leaders.priorTitle: Unknown (named after RMU's first national presidential search following Charles Sewall's retirement)
leaders.notes: Sixth president; led RMU's growth from a specialty business college into a broad-based university, including its 2002 renaming to Robert Morris University and creation of the first doctoral programs. The RMU student center is named for him.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for External Affairs (also formerly Dean of the business school)
leaders.notes: Seventh president, served ten years; left RMU in 2015 to become president of Rider University in New Jersey, from which he later announced retirement amid financial troubles.
RMU's long-serving provost stepped in as interim president from mid-2015 until Christopher Howard's arrival in February 2016, then resumed the provost role until 2019.

leaders.nextRole: Executive Leadership Team (Chief Executive, ASU Enterprise Partners)
leaders.notes: Eighth president and RMU's first African-American president; announced departure in January 2022 to join ASU's enterprise leadership team, with his exit effective around February 2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost / Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Briefly served as interim president and provost following Howard's departure (roughly Jan/Feb-April 2022) before retiring; succeeded in the interim role by Michelle Patrick.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, School of Business (RMU); previously Dean, College of Business and Public Management, West Chester University of Pennsylvania
leaders.notes: Named interim president in April 2022, then confirmed as RMU's ninth president in July 2022, becoming the first woman to lead the university in its history.

leaders.priorTitle: Academic administrator (prior posts included City College of New York, Pennsylvania State University, and SUNY Purchase)
leaders.priorInstitution: SUNY Purchase / City University of New York system
leaders.nextRole: President Emeritus; author of 'The Rise of Roosevelt University: Presidential Reflections'
leaders.notes: Fourth president; oversaw significant growth and expansion at Roosevelt. Remained active as president emeritus and memoirist until his death in 2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs, University System of Maryland (previously Provost, Bowling Green State University; and Dean of Arts and Sciences, University of Colorado Boulder)
leaders.nextRole: Chairman, Board of Trustees, City Colleges of Chicago; Executive Director, LGBTQ Presidents in Higher Education
leaders.notes: Fifth president; the first openly gay man appointed president of a university. Retired June 2015 and stayed active in higher-education leadership and LGBTQ advocacy roles.

Sixth president, started July 1, 2015. In March 2026 announced plans to retire at the conclusion of his contract on June 30, 2027, after 12 years of leadership; a presidential search is underway but he remains the sitting president as of this record.

statusNote: Formerly part of 'The Sage Colleges' system alongside Sage College of Albany and Sage Graduate School. Effective July 1, 2020, a charter change united Russell Sage College, Sage College of Albany, and Sage Graduate Schools into a single institution under the name Russell Sage College, operating as one college with two co-educational campuses (Troy and Albany, NY). In April 2025 a further merger with Albany College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences was announced, targeted for completion by Fall 2027.

leaders.notes: Seventh president of Russell Sage College; served through 1995, just prior to this index's normal start window but included since her term overlaps 1996 planning records used to establish successor dates.

Eighth president; announced retirement in January 2008 upon completing her 13th year as president, effective that June. A board-identified interim was expected to begin July 2008 pending a permanent successor; the interim's name could not be confirmed from available sources.

leaders.nextRole: Retired / continued as public health scholar and author
leaders.notes: Ninth president of The Sage Colleges (some sources cite an effective start in 2008); previously president of Simmons College (2006-2008). Announced she would step down in June 2017.

Tenth president, arrived July 2017; earlier served as provost/dean roles at Oglethorpe University and Washington College. Led the college's financial stabilization and the 2020 unification of the Sage Colleges under the single Russell Sage College name. Retired June 30, 2024.
11th president, began July 1, 2024; inaugurated that October alongside announcement of a $10 million gift to the college.

leaders.nextRole: President, National Catholic Educational Association / Continued Catholic higher-education consulting and advocacy work
leaders.notes: Fifth president; credited with growing SHU from near-bankruptcy into the second-largest Catholic university in New England over his 22-year tenure. Stepped down in October 2010.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, Jack Welch College of Business
leaders.notes: Served as interim president from October 2010 following Cernera's departure, then was named the university's sixth (permanent) president in March 2011.

leaders.priorTitle: Interim President (and Dean, Jack Welch College of Business); prior to SHU, Chancellor and CEO
leaders.priorInstitution: Seton Hall University and Immaculate Conception Seminary
leaders.notes: Sixth president, inaugurated 2011; before Sacred Heart he was chancellor/CEO of Seton Hall University and Immaculate Conception Seminary, and earlier led the University of Medicine and Dentistry of New Jersey. Still serving as of 2025 (testified before the Connecticut legislature that year as university president).
